scope: Independent semantic review of the frozen OOD-N04-B01 proposal snapshot only

identityConclusion.basis: All 18 mappings use the assigned new IDs and fresh option IDs. The replaced objects were generic owner-template questions, and the proposals introduce concrete contract decisions. The new ID assignments do not make duplicates of accepted N01 questions acceptable; replace the content under the proposed new IDs while preserving accepted N01 items.

groupFindings.criterion: BIZQ-01 section 4.1: one coherent decision per question; the package should not repeat an accepted item’s same decisive facts and answer.
groupFindings.finding: The N04 proposal and accepted N01 item both ask how to replace a recording when four stable-ID annotations map and one does not, and both require rejecting the replacement, keeping the old recording active, and naming the unmatched segment. This is a near-identical learner decision, not merely shared practice of interface contracts.
groupFindings.minimumCorrection: Replace the proposed N04-i023 scenario and decision under its proposed new ID. Preserve accepted N01-B02-i018 unchanged.

groupFindings.criterion: BIZQ-01 sections 4.1 and 4.3: a single-choice key must satisfy the visible retry contract and the new item should not materially repeat the accepted learner decision.
groupFindings.finding: Both questions use a stable payout identity after a timeout/retry, require the caller to learn whether the original payout completed, and prevent a duplicate payout by returning its original outcome/reference. The pending state is an added detail, but the central decision remains replay-safe payout retry and result reconciliation. In addition, the proposed key does not explicitly state that repeating the command with the same request ID is idempotent, while Details asserts it can be resubmitted safely.
groupFindings.minimumCorrection: Replace the proposed case with a materially distinct B01 contract decision, or refocus it on a distinct timeout-reconciliation decision and state the replay/idempotency guarantee in the key. Preserve accepted N01-B02-i021 unchanged.

groupFindings.criterion: BIZQ-01 section 4.3: alternatives should be comparably concrete and avoid a systematic cue that the longest option is correct.
groupFindings.finding: Using whitespace-separated words, the key is uniquely longest in 7/18 questions and tied for longest in 6/18. Some within-item gaps are large: i026 is 19 words versus a 10-word wrong option, i033 is 18 versus 8, and i036 is 17 versus 10. The keys often state the complete contract while distractors are short, generic, or overbroad.
groupFindings.minimumCorrection: Revise affected option sets so the wrong models are comparably plausible and specific, without padding them, imposing equal word counts, or changing the diagnosed mistakes.

itemFindings.finding: The key offers inspect and replace-assignment operations in one maintenance capability without scoping replacement to the swap caller; Details claims inspection has no mutator. Make the authority split explicit.
The visible dispatch/consent and audit/read-only facts support the keyed separate contracts; wrong-option diagnostics match their targets.
The immutable submitted versions and read-only history facts support the command/result and query boundary.
The named-manager/control condition and read-only queue fields support the proposed approval and query operations.
Near-identical primary decision and answer to accepted OOD-N01-B02-i018.
The resource screen needs a read-only effective-state query and the prompt withholds grant-edit authority.
The prompt explicitly binds sealing to the immutable revision and digest the signer confirmed.
Near-duplicate of accepted OOD-N01-B02-i021; the key also needs to state replay safety rather than leave it to Details.
Passenger query needs and controller-only correction authority are explicit and match the key.
The meter service’s reservation rule and caller’s required conflict result support the keyed API.
The shared caller-visible input, result, and startup-error facts support a common provider contract.
The keyed wrong-option feedback calls decision data sensitive although the prompt does not establish sensitivity; remove that unsupported claim.
The parent-revision and conflict-identity requirements support an owner-checked edit contract.
The selected ruleset and prohibition on quest mutation support the claim/evaluation boundary.
Both handoff checks and the read-only tracking role are visible and support the key.
The prompt explicitly separates a non-mutating preview from the posting operation.
The generic void() option that clears a final result is implausible filler under section 4.3; replace it with a credible distinct mistake and update its diagnostic.
Inspection evidence and separate refund-review authority are explicit and support the classification contract.

crossUnitNote: Shared practice of interface abstraction is valid. The two marked N01 overlaps are materially repeated decisions in the same OOD track; N03-B05 provider/dependency decisions share a broad concept with N04-i029 but ask a different concrete contract question.
limitations: Proposal semantic review only; no source activation, producer proof acceptance, consumer acceptance, native behavior, or full BIZQ-01 closure is claimed.
